title: Laptop Design Comparison Showcase
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D laptop design comparison showcase using Three.js.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a dark gradient background (top: #1a1a2e, bottom: #16213e).
- Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8 (warm white #fff5e6) and one from (-5, 5, -5) with intensity 0.4 (cool white #e6f0ff).
- Add a reflective floor plane at y=0, size 20x20, using MeshStandardMaterial with color #222233, metalness 0.8, roughness 0.3.

3D MODEL:
- Load 'collision-world.glb' using GLTFLoader from Three.js CDN. This model serves as the environment/stage backdrop.
- Scale the loaded model to fit within a 4x4x4 bounding box and position it at (0, 0, -3) behind the main display area.
- Set the model's material opacity to 0.3 and make it semi-transparent to serve as an atmospheric backdrop.

LAPTOP MODELS (Procedural):
- Create THREE procedural laptop models side by side, representing 3 design variants:
  - Laptop A ("UltraSlim"): Position (-3, 0.5, 0). Thin body (2.4 x 0.08 x 1.6), screen (2.3 x 1.5 x 0.03). Color: silver (#c0c0c0). Screen emissive blue (#0066ff).
  - Laptop B ("ProPower"): Position (0, 0.5, 0). Thicker body (2.6 x 0.15 x 1.8), screen (2.5 x 1.6 x 0.04). Color: dark gray (#404040). Screen emissive green (#00ff66).
  - Laptop C ("CreatorEdge"): Position (3, 0.5, 0). Medium body (2.5 x 0.12 x 1.7), screen (2.4 x 1.55 x 0.035). Color: rose gold (#b76e79). Screen emissive purple (#9933ff).
- Each laptop consists of a base (box) and a screen (box) hinged at the back edge of the base. The screen should start at a 110-degree open angle.

INTERACTION:
1. SELECTION: Click on a laptop to select it. The selected laptop should scale up to 1.3x and move up by 0.5 units (y). Others scale to 0.8x. A glowing ring (torus) appears under the selected laptop. Default selection is Laptop B.
2. ROTATION: When a laptop is selected, pressing LEFT/RIGHT arrow keys rotates it around Y-axis by 15 degrees per press.
3. LID CONTROL: Press UP arrow to open the lid more (increase angle by 10 deg, max 170 deg), DOWN arrow to close it (decrease by 10 deg, min 0 deg - fully closed).
4. COMPARISON MODE: A DOM button 'Compare All' toggles comparison mode. In this mode, all three laptops scale to 1.0, align at same Y, and rotate in sync slowly (auto-rotate at 0.5 rad/s).
5. COLOR THEME: A DOM button 'Toggle Theme' switches between dark mode and light mode (light: floor becomes #ddddee, background becomes light gradient #f0f0f5 to #e0e0ea).
6. SPECS PANEL: A DOM div shows specs for the selected laptop. Each laptop has: name, weight (UltraSlim: 0.95kg, ProPower: 2.1kg, CreatorEdge: 1.6kg), and thickness.

HUD/UI:
- Top-left: Title 'Laptop Design Comparison' in white, 20px font.
- Bottom-center: Three clickable DOM buttons labeled 'UltraSlim', 'ProPower', 'CreatorEdge' to select laptops.
- Top-right: 'Compare All' button and 'Toggle Theme' button.
- Right side panel (200px wide): Specs panel showing selected laptop info.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- selectedLaptop: 0, 1, or 2 (index of selected laptop, default 1)
- lidAngle: current lid angle in degrees of selected laptop (default 110)
- rotationY: cumulative Y rotation in radians of selected laptop
- compareMode: boolean (default false)
- darkTheme: boolean (default true)
- laptopScales: array of 3 numbers representing current scale of each laptop
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when collision-world.glb is loaded)
- laptopPositionsY: array of 3 numbers for Y positions of each laptop
- specsVisible: string - name of laptop shown in specs panel

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.

ANIMATION:
- Smooth transitions for scale and position changes (lerp over ~0.5 seconds).
- In compare mode, all laptops rotate together.
- Add subtle floating animation (sine wave on Y, amplitude 0.05, frequency 1Hz) to the selected laptop when not in compare mode.
physics_constraints: Lid angle must be clamped between 0 and 170 degrees. Laptop positions must not overlap (maintain minimum 2.5 unit spacing on X). Scale values must remain positive and within [0.5, 1.5]. All rotations must be NaN-free. Y positions must stay within [0, 3] range.
